PullRequest.Title: Move customization list scrollbar to pane edge
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- move the customizations list, migration page, and Tools section scrollbars to the outer pane edge
- make each panel own vertical spacing while its header, controls, and content own their horizontal inset
- give virtualized pages dedicated native scroll containers around their content roots
- preserve the existing centered maximum width without negative margins or synthetic width expansion
- fix the clipped Extension Tools section so every tool set remains reachable
- strengthen narrow fixtures with independently scrollable outer and nested lists

Fixes #335508

## Verification

- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/media/aiCustomizationManagement.css`
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/{aiCustomizationManagementEditor,toolsListWidget}.ts`
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/test/browser/componentFixtures/sessions/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.fixture.ts`
- 69 focused customization editor/list/Tools unit tests
- all migration fixtures, plus Agents standard/narrow, Skills, Tools standard/narrow/light/empty/browse, and MCP regression fixtures
- customization and migration nested-scroll assertions: Workspace items, outer sections, and User items scroll independently
- Extension Tools assertion: outer sections reach Extension Tools, its nested list reaches exact end, and Tool Set 8 is visible

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the AI Customizations editor on Agents/Skills/Instructions or Tools, including a narrow Agents window with many extension tool sets.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: DOM construction, section rendering, virtualized-list allocation, and the next-animation-frame layout must complete before the selected list is fully usable. The editor's existing migration refresh is launched without awaiting it, so its filesystem/agent-host discovery is off the Tools/prompts rendering critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discovers prompt files and existing migration candidates for enabled migration categories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to four category computations run in one Promise.all; the three file categories issue their existing prompt-list operations (2, 1, and 3 calls respectively), subject to enabled-category filtering and service-level caching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same refresh and category fan-out ran before this diff; the changed code only restructures DOM scroll hosts and CSS widths/insets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The refresh is fire-and-forget during editor initialization, so it does not block Tools/prompts rendering; its result is required only for migration state/counts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Computes MCP-server migration eligibility using existing agent-host support state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one MCP migration computation per refresh alongside the enabled file-category computations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unchanged; no added call or scheduling change in this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the selected Tools/prompts page's immediate render critical path because initialization does not await refreshCustomizationMigrationInfo.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible customization sections and tool-set rows. Virtualized section layout is linear in the small number of sections and row-height aggregation is linear in entries during scheduled layout, as before; the diff adds only one wrapper element per affected list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Section layout requests remain coalesced by MutableDisposable onto one next-animation-frame callback. Existing migration category computations remain parallelized by Promise.all; the diff adds no concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache keys, invalidation, negative caching, or coalescing behavior changes. Scroll state is held by the existing DomScrollableElement; warm and cold page opens use the same service behavior as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed constructors, layout helpers, scrollable implementation, and service call paths were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual tool-set and migration-candidate counts vary, but the changed work is constant per scroll host and does not multiply existing discovery calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra wrappers and width rules do not add scaling boundary work or eager service calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll the Tools inventory or a customization migration category with enough sections to overflow the pane.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each wheel/scroll input updates the native scrollTop and overlay scrollbar position. No virtualized-row layout, DOM rebuild, filesystem work, IPC, or network request is scheduled by the added scroll listeners.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scroll-event frequency and content height. Each added listener performs one scrollTop read and one constant-time setScrollPosition; Scrollable._setState exits immediately when the browser event reflects the already-current position.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser scroll events are serialized on the UI thread. Layout remains separately coalesced to the next animation frame and is not triggered by these listeners.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. DomScrollableElement retains only current dimensions and position; the added disposable listeners are released with their owning editor/widget.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the event path was traced through DomScrollableElement.setScrollPosition and Scrollable._setState.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: High-frequency touchpad input can generate many events, but direct inspection proves the synchronization is O(1), state-equality suppresses duplicate emissions, and the same pattern is established in adjacent customization lists.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable synchronous-UI regression. The bridge neither creates a feedback loop nor performs layout/allocation per scroll event.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize the customization pane while Tools or a migration category is visible.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resize observation schedules section measurement and WorkbenchList layout for the next animation frame, followed by one scanDomNode to update overlay scrollbar dimensions.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible virtualized sections and entries used to aggregate row heights. The wrapper change does not increase section or entry cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tools and migration layout callbacks are each coalesced to a single pending animation-frame disposable, preserving prior backpressure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes. Existing per-section scroll positions are preserved across layout as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both schedule/layout paths and ResizeObserver ownership were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Pane resize frequency depends on user interaction, but the diff does not add observers or extra layout callbacks; it changes only the measured scroll target.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable layout regression. Work remains frame-coalesced and has the same collection scaling as before.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or search the Tools Marketplace browse view after the gallery container's width rule changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Entering browse mode waits for the existing gallery query and manifest filtering before rows appear; the CSS width change affects only rendering geometry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queries the extensions gallery and fetches manifests for first-page candidates to retain tool-contributing extensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One gallery query per browse entry or debounced search, followed by up to one manifest fetch per first-page extension via Promise.all; all cardinality and grouping are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, browse entry and debounced searches executed the identical query/filter path; only the gallery container width/margin selector changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing network calls are on the Marketplace results critical path, but the diff neither introduces them nor changes when or how often they run.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: First-page extension count after the single gallery query; effective network fan-out is unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Search remains debounced by 200 ms with cancellation of the prior query; manifest filtering remains the existing Promise.all fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The PR does not add or bypass a cache and does not alter query text, cancellation, or result reuse behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: browse-mode triggers and the complete query/filter call path were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Gallery page size and manifest cache warmth vary, but the changed CSS has no causal effect on boundary count or latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable network or rendering regression caused by the PR.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and every diff page. Traced scroll synchronization, virtualized layout/resize paths, editor initialization, migration discovery, and Marketplace boundaries. The DOM/CSS restructuring adds constant-size wrappers and O(1) scroll-state synchronization, preserves animation-frame coalescing and disposal, and introduces no scaling boundary calls or actionable performance regression.
